description: The Lou is Saint Laurent's compact camera bag, a slim quilted crossbody with a boxy shape, a zip top, and the metal Cassandre YSL logo on the front. Worn on a long adjustable strap, it is one of the house's most accessible everyday leather bags under Anthony Vaccarello. Our sourcing on its exact debut year is thin, so we leave it unset rather than guess. Do not confuse it with the larger chain-strap LouLou, which is a separate model.
note: Distinct from the YSL LouLou; Lou camera bag debut year not cleanly sourced.

description: The Reissue is Chanel's faithful re-edition of Coco Chanel's original February 1955 2.55 flap, brought back by Karl Lagerfeld in 2005 to mark the design's 50th anniversary. It is set apart from the Classic Flap by its details: the rectangular Mademoiselle turn-lock instead of the interlocking CC, an all-metal chain woven through the strap, and an aged or quilted calfskin body. The base 2.55 design dates to 1955, while this reissued version dates to 2005. Chanel numbers it by size, from the 224 up through 227 and larger.
note: Likely the 2.55 Reissue; probable duplicate of style 423 (Chanel 2.55). Base 2.55 = Feb 1955; the Reissue re-edition debuted 2005.

description: The Puzzle is Loewe's geometric cuboid bag, built from precisely cut leather panels that fold flat and open into a boxy three-dimensional shape. It was Jonathan Anderson's first bag for the house, debuting in 2014, and the first entirely new Loewe bag design in decades. Worn crossbody or by the top handle, it is defined by its architectural seams and folds rather than any logo hardware.

The Coco Handle, officially the Flap Bag with Top Handle, is a structured quilted flap fitted with a single rigid top handle and the CC turn-lock closure. Chanel introduced it around 2015, often trimmed with woven or exotic-look detailing near the handle. It reads as a more ladylike, hand-carried take on the Classic Flap and is offered in caviar and lambskin across several sizes. Sources vary on the exact debut, citing 2015 to 2017.

The Deauville is Chanel's canvas shopping tote, introduced in the Spring/Summer 2012 collection and named for the French seaside resort. It is a large open two-handle tote, most iconically in grosgrain or heavyweight canvas with leather trim, a reinforced base, and a bold CC logo on the front. Reissued nearly every season since, it is Chanel's go-to casual daytime and travel tote.

The Twist is Louis Vuitton's leather shoulder flap, named for its signature closure: an oversized LV lock whose two letters physically turn to open. It was one of Nicolas Ghesquière's early designs for the house, arriving in 2015, usually made in smooth Epi leather with a chain-and-leather strap. It comes in several sizes and countless seasonal finishes, sitting as one of LV's core leather rather than canvas bags.

The Classic City, Balenciaga's motorcycle bag, is the slouchy lightweight shoulder bag that defined mid-2000s It-bag culture. Designed under Nicolas Ghesquière, it grew out of his earlier First and Lariat prototypes and is recognizable by its buttery distressed lambskin, front zip pocket, whipstitched handles, and buckle-and-stud hardware with a mirror and leather tassels on the zip pulls. It carries with both handles or a detachable shoulder strap. The motorcycle line launched in the early 2000s, with the City version dated variously between 2001 and 2003.
note: Motorcycle line debuted ~2000 (First/Lariat); City version dated variously 2001-2003, so year held null.

description: The Pouch is Bottega Veneta's soft, oversized clutch, created by Daniel Lee and introduced in 2019. It is a frame-top bag with a ruched, pillowy body in supple nappa leather, deliberately logo-free and gathered into a cinched middle. It became a defining bag of Lee's minimalist, quiet-luxury Bottega and helped drive the brand's late-2010s revival.

The NéoNoé is Louis Vuitton's modern bucket bag, introduced in 2017 as a reworking of the original 1932 Noé, which was first built to carry champagne bottles. It keeps the drawstring-cinched bucket shape but adds an adjustable leather strap, a contrasting interior, and a rounded body, most often in Monogram or Damier canvas with leather trim. It is offered in the standard NéoNoé and the smaller BB size.

The Saint-Louis is Goyard's signature tote and its most recognizable bag, a lightweight, unlined, reversible shopping tote in the hand-painted Goyardine chevron canvas. Sotheby's dates the design to the 1930s, when it was conceived as a beach bag, which makes it far older than the resellers' usual comparison, the 2007 Louis Vuitton Neverfull. It has no closure and almost no metal hardware, just leather handles and trim, and comes in PM and GM sizes. Because a clean single launch year is not documented, we leave the year unset.
note: Sotheby's dates it to the 1930s (decade, not a clean year), so year held null.

description: The Soho Disco is Gucci's round-cornered crossbody, a lightweight zip-top camera bag in soft pebbled leather with an embossed interlocking-GG logo and a slim tassel zip pull. Designed under Frida Giannini, it launched in the early 2010s and became one of Gucci's most popular accessible bags. Sources place its debut around 2011 to 2012, so we hold the exact year open.
note: Frida Giannini era; debut cited 2011-2012, so year held null.

description: The Sac de Jour is Saint Laurent's structured top-handle tote, introduced in 2013 under Hedi Slimane. It is a crisply architectural bag with two rolled top handles, a removable shoulder strap, winged sides that fold in, and the metal YSL Cassandre logo on the front. Made in smooth or grained calfskin across several sizes, it is the house's answer to the ladylike structured tote and one of its modern classics.

Le 5 à 7 is Saint Laurent's clean-lined shoulder hobo, introduced in the Spring 2021 collection under Anthony Vaccarello and named for the French idiom for an early-evening rendezvous. It is a smooth, structured half-moon shape that sits under the arm on a single strap, closed with the metal YSL Cassandre logo and deliberately minimal on hardware. It comes in several sizes and quickly became a modern signature for the house.

The Coussin is Louis Vuitton's puffy, cushion-soft bag, introduced in 2021 under Nicolas Ghesquière. Its body is quilted in oversized puffy Monogram embossing on lambskin, finished with a chunky chain strap and an LV padlock charm. It comes in PM and larger sizes and reads as LV's plush, pillow-like answer to the quilted-chain bag.

The Chanel 25 is the house's big 2025 debut, a soft, hobo-inspired flap named for its year of release. It has a supple, lightly slouched body, two signature side pockets, and a relaxed everyday shape, offered in small, medium, and large. It joins Chanel's numbered icon line alongside the 19 and the 22 as a modern, un-fussy daily bag.

The Bolide is Hermès's domed, structured carryall and is famous as the first leather bag to use a zipper, introduced in 1923 after Émile-Maurice Hermès secured French rights to the fastening. Designed originally for automobile travel, it has a rounded top, a trapezoidal body, two handles, and a zip that follows the curve of the bag, often with a shoulder strap. It comes in many sizes and leathers and is one of the house's oldest continuously made designs.

Bamboo 1947 is Gucci's revival of its original bamboo-handled bag, a top-handle design the house first created in 1947 using heat-bent bamboo when leather was scarce in postwar Italy. Alessandro Michele reintroduced it as the Bamboo 1947 for Gucci's 2021 Aria collection, keeping the curved bamboo handle and turn-lock while updating the proportions. The name marks the year of the original design.
note: Original bamboo bag = 1947; the 'Bamboo 1947' reissue debuted 2021 (Aria collection).

description: The Diana is Gucci's bamboo-handle tote, first presented in 1991 and made famous by Princess Diana, whose name it now carries. It pairs a structured leather body with two bamboo top handles held by the house's signature leather belt straps that wrap the base of each handle. Alessandro Michele reintroduced it in 2021 with removable neon and colored leather belts, and it is offered in several sizes.

The Rockstud is Valentino's stud-covered line, introduced in 2010 under Maria Grazia Chiuri and Pierpaolo Piccioli and defined by rows of pale gold pyramid studs running along the edges of the bags and matching shoes. It spans flaps, totes, and crossbodies in smooth calfskin, with the studs as the constant signature. Note that Valentino's later Roman Stud, launched in 2020, is a distinct, quilted big-stud evolution rather than the same bag.
note: Rockstud line = 2010; distinct from the Roman Stud (2020).

description: The Chanel 22 is a slouchy, oversized shopping-tote-style bag introduced in 2022 under Virginie Viard and named for its release year. It has a soft, puffed body in quilted calfskin, grommeted top edges threaded with a chain-and-leather strap, and a hanging CC medallion charm. Offered in small through large, it reads as a relaxed, modern hobo counterpoint to the structured Classic Flap.

The Garden Party is Hermès's casual open tote, a roomy trapezoidal shopper with two rolled handles and, most often, a canvas body trimmed in leather or an all-leather build. Sotheby's dates the design to 1964, when it grew out of the house's equestrian world before becoming an everyday carry-all. It closes with a simple snap and comes in sizes like the 30 and 36, sitting as one of Hermès's most accessible and hardworking totes. Treat the year as approximate, since some accounts date the modern tote later.
note: Sotheby's dates it to 1964; some accounts date the modern tote later, so year is approximate.

description: The Pochette Accessoires is Louis Vuitton's small flat pouch, introduced in 1992 originally as an inner organizer for the house's larger bags before becoming a standalone mini bag. It is a slim zip-top pouch, most iconic in Monogram canvas with a short wrist strap, and has been reworked in collaborations like the Stephen Sprouse graffiti version. It is one of LV's most collected small accessories and a frequent gateway piece.

The Antigona is Givenchy's structured tote, introduced in 2011 under Riccardo Tisci and named after the mythological figure Antigone. It has a crisply geometric, winged silhouette with a zip top, two rolled handles, and a removable strap, most recognizable in smooth grained calfskin with the Givenchy logo stamped on the front. It comes in mini through large sizes and became the defining bag of Tisci's tenure at the house.

The Jet Set is Michael Kors's signature everyday line, best known as the Jet Set Travel tote: a lightweight saffiano-leather tote or crossbody with a top zip and the metal MK logo on the front. It is the brand's most recognizable accessible-luxury bag and comes in totes, crossbodies, and multifunction styles across many sizes. We could not cleanly source a single introduction year, so we leave it unset.
note: Signature line; no clean debut year sourced.

description: The Belt bag is Celine's soft, structured bag from the Phoebe Philo era, created for Spring 2015. It is defined by the long knotted leather strap that wraps and ties around the front, a winged, slightly trapezoidal body, and a top-handle carry with an optional shoulder strap. Pared back and logo-free, it sits alongside the Luggage and Trapeze as a signature Philo-era Celine and was retired when the house discontinued the old-Celine bags.
note: Phoebe Philo era; retired when Celine discontinued the Philo-era bags.
